Course overview
COURSE OVERVIEW
Scope
This course introduces the fundamental
concepts of electric power systems
engineering.
Primary focus
Modeling power-system components
and studying an interconnected system
under steady-state conditions.
1 Describe the physical equipment
and network.
2 Build consistent mathematical
models.
3 Use analysis to support a design
decision.
The course moves from individual components to a defensible system-level
recommendation.
ECE 685 | Course Orientation & Logistics 5/27

Course goals
COURSE GOALS AND LEARNING OUTCOMES
1 Compute power flows in
three-phase circuits.
2 Model transformers and
transmission lines.
3 Solve power systems using the
per-unit method.
4 Compare power-generation
alternatives economically.
5 Perform and interpret PowerWorld
power-flow simulations.
6 Recognize social and
environmental issues associated
with power systems.

Responsible AI use
CONSTRUCTIVE USE AND REQUIRED CHECKS
Encouraged
clarify concepts;
explore alternative approaches;
support coding, writing, and
checking.
Required
verify every result;
explain every submitted claim;
disclose the tool and its
contribution.
AI may accelerate a step; it may not replace your understanding.
ECE 685 | Course Orientation & Logistics 19/27

Prohibited AI use
ACADEMIC INTEGRITY
1 Treating an AI answer as automatically correct.
2 Submitting material AI contribution without disclosure.
3 Using unauthorized AI assistance on an exam or restricted assignment.
A useful disclosure names the tool, the task it supported, and how the result was
verified.

Power-system history
A SHORT HISTORICAL PERSPECTIVE
1882 - Pearl Street
A local DC system served 85
customers within roughly one
square mile.
1884 - Early AC transmission
Transformer-based AC
demonstrated practical power
transfer over a much longer
distance.
T oday’s interconnected networks coordinate
many generators, transmission paths, and
loads across regions.
ECE 685 | Course Orientation & Logistics 23/27

Primary
energy
Gener-
ation
Trans-

Distri-

The grid is an energy-delivery system and an information-and-control system at the
same time.
ECE 685 | Course Orientation & Logistics 24/27

Grid transformation
TRADITIONAL STRUCTURE AND EMERGING OPERATION
Traditional structure
large central generating plants;
predominantly one-way delivery;
limited visibility near end users.
Evolving structure
renewable generation and storage;
bidirectional power flows;
more sensors, communication, and
automated control.
New technology changes where power enters the network and how operators observe
and control it.
ECE 685 | Course Orientation & Logistics 25/27

Reliability challenge
THE ENGINEERING CHALLENGE
1 Balance electricity production and
consumption continuously.
2 Keep voltages, currents, and
equipment loading within limits.
3 Withstand equipment outages,
weather, and other disturbances.
4 Adapt generation and transmission
economically as needs change.
Every grid transition must preserve reliable service while expanding capability.
ECE 685 | Course Orientation & Logistics 26/27

Design workflow
BRIDGE TO LECTURE 02
1 Represent the connected
physical system with
consistent data.
2 Solve the mathematical
model under defined
conditions.
3 Check limits, balances, and
operating credibility.
Lecture 02 begins with the equipment and one-line vocabulary used to build that
model.
